references.text: Also describes the boundary that goes up from the Jordan at Jericho, using similar geographical terminology
Mentions Jericho in connection with the boundary description for the tribe of Ephraim
Mentions Beth-Aven, the same place noted as the endpoint of the boundary in this text
Hosea mentions Beth-Aven as a site of idolatry, the same place where the boundary ends
Beth-Aven is mentioned again in Hosea as a geographical reference point
Mentions Beth-Aven in connection with Israel's history
Describes a similar boundary area that goes up toward the north, using parallel terminology
